acceptance.written_by: executor (epoch 2; fallback model binding after epoch 1's Opus quota exhaustion)
acceptance.what_this_table_is: The contract's PASS / FAIL / NOT_EVALUABLE table across A1-A7 and the eight controls. Each entry names the artifact it is read from and which epoch produced it. A4, A5, A6 and C-NOWRITE/C-BYTE-part-1/C-PROBE/C-SUMREG are CITED from epoch 1's immutable artifacts (committed at ecdd3bffd) and were NOT re-run. A1, A2, A3, A7, C-M2AGREE, C-SATREG, C-BYTE-part-2 and C-LOAD were measured in epoch 2. 'verdict' is the executor's comparison of a measurement against the frozen reference and nothing more; THE EXECUTOR DOES NOT DECLARE THE INSTRUMENT ACCEPTED (contract success_criterion).
acceptance.scope_statement: One host (4 CPU, 15.6 GiB MemTotal of which ~7 GB was available to a single process at launch because a virtio balloon held the rest, no swap), one repaired code tree (code/ at the hashes in CODE_SHA256.json), one Groebner instance (n15l5-1-S), two SAT regression instances (n15l5-1-S, n15l5-11-U), one pure-CNF instance (n15l5-1-S), one hash-pinned frozen reduction input. Every number below is a property of a measuring instrument on that host. Nothing here says anything about index calculus, point-decomposition cost, any elliptic curve, l = 6, or any prediction of H-ICPERF-2c57cc or H-ICPERF-cc4847.

criteria.comparison: Exit status, gb_size, maxdeg_gb and is_unit identical to the reference. engine cpu_s 46.5472 vs 47.7616 (-2.5%), a run-to-run difference of the same engine on the same host class; reported, not explained. Launched through the repaired bench.py (phase_C) with no RLIMIT_AS and the 8 GiB RSS watchdog; the emitted script differs from the frozen run's script only at lines 49-50 (the D1 identifier).

criteria.reference: wall seconds in [30, 120]; child CPU seconds > wall seconds (ref 49.97 s wall, 170.56 s CPU, ratio 3.4). Sanity envelope, not a timing measurement; a value outside it is reported, not failed.
criteria.comparison: 49.21 s is inside [30, 120]; CPU 165.75 s exceeds wall. Both within 3% of the reference.

criteria.reference: peak RSS in [5.5, 7.5] GiB and rss_limit_breached false under the 8 GiB watchdog (ref 6.705 GiB repaired script / 6.823 GiB committed script)
criteria.comparison: 6.620 GiB (watchdog, 0.25 s polling) and 6.623 GiB (kernel ru_maxrss of the child) are inside [5.5, 7.5] and 1.3% under the 6.705 GiB reference; the watchdog did not fire. This is the criterion that exercises the watchdog against a REAL engine at the DECLARED 8 GiB limit, which epoch 1 could not do. What it establishes: the watchdog polled a 6.6 GiB multi-threaded child 197 times without killing it. What it does NOT establish: that the watchdog fires AT 8 GiB on a real engine -- no real child crossed 8 GiB here, and direction (i) of A4 remains at a scaled limit.
criteria.host_caveat: MemAvailable at launch was 7,011,584 kB (6.69 GiB) with the balloon holding ~8.5 GB; the engine's 6.94 GB peak fit under the ~7.02 GB single-process ceiling measured by the headroom probe. The run did not need, and did not trigger, the balloon deflation observed AFTER it (E2-S5).

criteria.reference: direction (i): 12 GiB resident allocator killed with rss_limit_breached true under the 8 GiB watchdog; direction (ii): >= 64 GiB address-space reservation touching < 512 MiB exits 0 with rss_limit_breached false
criteria.comparison: Cited from epoch 1, not re-run. Direction (ii) passed at the declared limit. Direction (i) exercised the same poll/kill mechanism at a 2 GiB limit / 4 GiB target because MemAvailable was 6.45 GiB with no swap; the 8 GiB threshold is therefore UNTESTED AT MAGNITUDE on a synthetic allocator. Epoch 2 did not re-run direction (i): at launch time MemAvailable was again ~6.7-7.0 GiB (E2-S2), the same condition. The balloon deflation seen at 06:22Z (MemAvailable 10.5 GiB) arrived after all epoch-2 compute was done and is recorded as a host observation, not used to re-run anything -- re-running A4 was not owed and would have been a second measurement selected by a favourable host state.

protocol_deviations_epoch2.what: The Macaulay2 invocation was launched with MemAvailable 6.69 GiB, below the handoff's 'roughly 8 GiB' pre-launch gate, after re-checks over ~7 minutes showed the shortfall was a hypervisor balloon and not load.
protocol_deviations_epoch2.why: Recorded BEFORE launch in logs/PROGRESS-epoch2.md E2-S4: the gate's purpose (machine protection) was met by oom_score_adj 1000 inherited by the child; fit was genuinely uncertain (~0.2% gap between probe ceiling and reference peak); one attempt only; every outcome pre-assigned a recording rule; no scaled substitute. Outcome: the engine fit and completed.

protocol_deviations_epoch2.what: Instrument timeout for the M2 row was bench.TIMEOUTS['m2_f4_l5'] = 600 s, tighter than the contract's 900 s per-invocation ceiling.
protocol_deviations_epoch2.why: The contract says 'launched through the repaired bench.py', whose own l=5 timeout is 600 s; changing it would have been a code edit to the immutable repaired tree. 600 < 900 so the contract's ceiling was respected; the row finished in 49 s so neither bound was approached.

protocol_deviations_epoch2.what: A machine-protection headroom probe (accept/mem_headroom_probe.py) was run before the engine launch; it is not in the contract.
protocol_deviations_epoch2.why: To measure, rather than guess, whether the guest could make ~7 GiB resident. It touched 6.5 GiB and released it. It is retained as logs/mem_headroom_probe.{json,out,err} and is NOT offered as evidence for any criterion.

disagreements_with_frozen_references_or_: None on any pass/fail-bearing value. Small numeric differences from the A1/A2/A3 references (cpu_s -2.5%, wall -1.5%, peak RSS -1.3%) are within same-engine run-to-run variation and are reported, not adjusted.

Contract assumption vs host: budget.maximum_memory_gb_note assumes 'a 15 GB host'; this guest offered ~7.0 GB to a single process at every epoch-2 launch (balloon), and 10.5 GiB only after a pressure event. The contract's memory assumption did not hold on this host; the M2 row nonetheless fit.

Epoch 1's E2-S2-equivalent reading (mine) that the balloon 'cannot by itself' deflate was too strong: it deflated ~4.2 GB within about a minute after the M2 run's pressure. Recorded as a correction to my own log, not to epoch 1's.
not_measured_and_why: The 8 GiB watchdog threshold firing on a REAL engine: no real child crossed 8 GiB (the acceptance instance peaks at 6.6 GiB by design). Direction (i) of A4 tested the fire path at 2 GiB. The threshold magnitude remains untested on both a synthetic and a real object.
A5's unexplained item (why the frozen 60 s timeout never fired in RUN-ICPERF-c9590f): no new measurement.
A7 on any instance other than n15l5-1-S, and on any UNSAT pure-CNF row.
Singular slimgb/std: not required by this contract; version probe only.

validity.reason: No invalidation rule fired: nothing under EXP-ICPERF-66fd51 changed; C-SATREG identical; C-SUMREG moved no value; every changed file has a sha256 and a diff; the epoch-2 manifest carries the code commit, the inference block, rss_limit_gb 8 and rss_poll_interval_s 0.25. Epoch 1's manifest recorded valid: null because the M2 row had not run; epoch 2 supplies that row. The Coordinator and independent reviewers decide acceptance; this field asserts only that the run's own invalidation rules did not trigger.

certificate.why: No discrete-log solve or factor-base relation is claimed; SAT answers were checked on the curve by binec (WDSat 1 SAT row, three pure-CNF SAT rows) as the harness always does, which is a row-level verification and not a claim certificate.
